narrative.overview: PurpleInk should feel like a release team reviewing the final cut on calibrated screens: focused, authored, factual, and ready to publish. The visual language combines a decisive purple field with near-black review surfaces, pale product canvases, and explicit proof states.
keyCharacteristics: Committed purple, disciplined by ink, paper, proof green, and signal coral.
Product evidence is the primary imagery; decorative effects never replace proof.
Flat narrative bands and tonal layering; shadows are rare and structural.
Manrope carries the message; Azeret Mono is metadata-only.
Compact controls, moderate corners, explicit focus, and no nested cards.

rules.name: Proof Before Promise
rules.body: Every visual claim must point to a visible product frame, source record, checkpoint, or clearly labeled prototype.

rules.name: Three-Voice
rules.body: On ordinary screens, use one brand color, one semantic color only when state requires it, and the neutral system.

rules.name: Color Is Not Evidence
rules.body: Verified, warning, and blocked states always include text or an icon in addition to color.

rules.name: Tracking Floor
rules.body: Display tracking never goes below -0.04em. Body and controls always use zero letter spacing.

rules.name: Metadata Boundary
rules.body: Mono type is reserved for machine-readable context.

rules.name: Flat By Default
rules.body: Surfaces remain flat at rest. Never combine a decorative border with a large diffuse shadow.

dos: Lead with product proof, attached sources, approval state, and reproducible workflow.
Use Directed Purple for brand/action, Verified Green for proof, and Review Coral for intervention only.
Pair every semantic color with an icon or text label.
donts: Do not present PurpleInk as a generic prompt-to-video or AI design generator.
Do not build a purple-gradient SaaS template or invent product evidence.
Do not use gradient text, decorative color orbs, glass cards, or nested cards.
Do not use white normal-sized text on dark-purple; use ink-panel text instead.
